issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires using only local buffers for input and forbids global symbols for buffers (lines 35-36). Both the template and the solution declare a global input buffer in .bss (buf resb 16) and the template even exports it with a 'global buf' directive (template: line 31). This contradicts the requirement and may confuse students: they are told not to use global buffers but are given one in the template/solution (and the template's explicit 'global' export makes the buffer a global symbol). Students may follow the template and violate the exercise constraints, or be unsure whether the global buffer is allowed.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the artifacts consistent with the specification. Either (A) remove the global input buffer and the 'global buf' export from the template and solution, and change code to allocate a local buffer on the stack (e.g. reserve 16 bytes in main via sub esp,16 or use [ebp-16]) and pass its address to fgets/atoi; or (B) if providing a global buffer is intentional, update the problem statement to allow a global input buffer. Option A preserves the original educational intent (forcing use of local buffers) and avoids exporting 'buf' as a global symbol.
